newsitem.title: USA: Dollar at new highs as data soothes inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: Dollar at new highs as data soothes inflation fears.

text.p: The dollar set a high against the German mark for the fifth consecutive session Tuesday and rose to a 45-month peak versus the Japanese yen after U.S. economic data soothed fears about inflation.
The dollar surged to 1.5973 marks, its highest level since July 1994, following the release of subdued U.S. consumer price and retail sales figures for December.

"I think the dollar continues to benefit from strong economic growth and the perception of moderate to weak inflation in the United States," said John Nelson, a senior vice president at ABN-AMRO Bank in New York.

The Labour Department reported consumer prices gained only 0.1 percent for the month, below Wall Street's expectation of a 0.2 percent rise. Simultaneously, the Commerce Department reported December retail sales grew by 0.6 percent, slightly above the consensus forecast of a 0.5 percent rise.
Comments from German central bank council members and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin aided the dollar, along with strong rallies in U.S. stock and bond markets.
Bundesbank Council Member Helmut Hess warned on Tuesday that the mark could weaken in the approach to the European monetary union as investors may switch their funds into other currencies.
Traders interpreted Hesse's remark at a reception as an effort to mute market speculation that the European central banks will intervene at current levels to support the value of the mark.

His collegue Olaf Sievert, a council member and president of the regional central bank based in Liepzig, also brightened the dollar's prospects. He said Germany's central bank will have no grounds to raise interest rates near-term and may even lower credit costs later this economic cycle.
In the United States, Rubin, for a second straight day, spoke out in support of a strong dollar. But his remarks had little impact after giving the dollar a major boost on Monday.
The dollar rose to 1.5941 marks in late trading from 1.5887 late Monday. The dollar inched lower to 1.3748 Swiss francs from 1.3758 late Monday.
Against the yen, the dollar made a late push to break its earlier 117.04 high, but closed just shy at 116.93. The dollar ended Monday's session at 116.48 yen.

"A lot of people are very cautious about breaking above the 117 level, fearing Bank of Japan or Ministry of Finance intervention (to support the yen)," said Jeffrey Yu, a senior trader at Sanwa Bank Ltd. in New York.
The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3516 from C$1.3473 at Monday's close.
